label: National Ignition Facility (NIF)
sub: Achieved fusion ignition Dec 5, 2022. Confirmed record: 8.6 MJ yield, gain 4.13x, from 2.08 MJ laser input (8th ignition, Apr 7, 2025) — supersedes the earlier 5.2 MJ (Feb 2024) figure. EYC laser upgrade (2.2→2.6 MJ) cleared CD-1 April 24, 2026. Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Livermore, CA.

label: Inertia — Livermore, CA
sub: Opened 50,000 sq ft HQ July 10, 2026 housing the world's first fusion fuel target factory plus a high-precision metrology facility, commercializing ICF breakthroughs from nearby NIF. Targeting end-to-end fuel-capsule production by 2027; power-plant groundbreaking targeted 2030. $450M+ raised (Feb 2026 fundraise).

label: ITER — Cadarache, France
sub: 35-nation international tokamak. First plasma now scheduled 2033. Sixth of nine tokamak sector modules installed Jul 28, 2026 — two-thirds of plasma chamber now in place, ~6 months ahead of Baseline 2024 schedule. Budget: €20B+.

label: Commonwealth Fusion Systems — Devens, MA
sub: SPARC ~80% assembled (all 18 magnets expected by end of summer 2026), first plasma targeted 2027. First fusion company to apply to PJM grid interconnection (Apr 28, 2026). $4B total raised after $1B round (Jul 30, 2026) — first pension-fund investment in fusion; eyeing IPO in 2-3 years. MIT spinoff.

label: Helion Energy HQ — Everett, WA
sub: Helion corporate HQ. Polaris (7th prototype) achieved 150M°C D-T plasma (Feb 2026). $1.5B total raised; $15.5B valuation (Jun 4, 2026 Series G). Microsoft PPA: 50 MW by 2028. Orion commercial plant under construction in Malaga, WA.

label: Helion Orion Plant — Malaga, WA
sub: Helion's first commercial fusion power plant under construction. Targeting 50 MW delivery to Microsoft by 2028. Backed by $465M Series G (Jun 2026). Field-reversed configuration, direct energy conversion.

label: Pacific Fusion — Fremont, CA
sub: Pulsed-power inertial confinement fusion startup. 440 GW subscale pulser prototype milestone (Jun 2, 2026). LLNL-built Sirius prototype surpassed 3,000 shots on the same IMG architecture (Jul 16, 2026), 95% energy efficiency. $1B+ Series A (tranche-based). Demo facility construction begins summer 2026. Also building $1B fusion campus in New Mexico.

label: Focused Energy — Biblis, Germany
sub: German laser-ICF startup building the world's first commercial laser-fusion plant at the Biblis nuclear site near Frankfurt. $240M Series A (May 27, 2026, led by RWE); $300M total raised + $200M grants. Approach builds directly on NIF ignition platform.

label: Thea Energy — Princeton, NJ
sub: Princeton University spinout developing planar-coil optimized stellarators. $130M raised (Series B, May 27, 2026), led by Thomas Tull's US Innovative Technology Fund + Idemitsu. Won $20M ARPA-E SCALEUP award (Jul 27, 2026) to build first domestic HTS magnet manufacturing lines for the ~300-coil 'Eos' stellarator. DOE Helios preconceptual design certification. Second NJ manufacturing facility planned for magnet production.

label: KSTAR — Daejeon, South Korea
sub: World record: 48 seconds at 100M°C (Apr 2024). Targeting 300 seconds by 2026. Korea Institute of Fusion Energy.

label: EAST Tokamak — Hefei, China
sub: World record 1,066-second plasma at 100M°C (Jan 20, 2025). Institute of Plasma Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences.

label: JT-60SA — Naka, Japan
sub: World's largest operational superconducting tokamak. First plasma Dec 1, 2023. Completed major upgrades May 2026 (new first wall, in-vessel coils, heating systems); integrated commissioning underway — plasma experiments expected late 2026. Japan-EU Broader Approach joint project.

label: Wendelstein 7-X — Greifswald, Germany
sub: World's largest stellarator. Demonstrates steady-state plasma confinement. Max-Planck-Institut für Plasmaphysik.

label: WEST Tokamak — Cadarache, France
sub: World record 1,337-second plasma (Feb 2025). Tests all-tungsten first wall for ITER. CEA / Institut de Recherche sur la Fusion Magnétique.

label: MIT Plasma Science & Fusion Center — Cambridge, MA
sub: Birthplace of CFS. Developed REBCO HTS magnet technology achieving 20 Tesla (Sep 2021). Dennis Whyte, Bob Mumgaard alumni.

label: TAE Technologies — Foothill Ranch, CA
sub: Hydrogen-boron (p-B11) aneutronic fusion. Norman machine. $1.3B+ raised. Google partnership since 2014. Signed helium-3 fuel supply agreement with Black Moon Energy (Aug 5, 2026) as an alternative fuel path. Da Vinci power plant (50 MWe) targets operations in 2031.

label: General Fusion — Richmond, BC, Canada
sub: Magnetized target fusion (MTF). $492M raised. Targeting public markets via SPAC merger (2026). Backed by Bezos, Temasek.

label: STEP — West Burton A, Nottinghamshire, UK
sub: UK's Spherical Tokamak for Energy Production. £1.3B National Fusion Strategy (Apr 2026); total £2.5B committed (2025–2030). ILIOS Consortium awarded £200M construction partner contract. Operations target: 2040. UKAEA / West Burton A, Nottinghamshire.

label: Culham Centre for Fusion Energy — Abingdon, UK
sub: Home of JET (Joint European Torus, decommissioned 2024). UKAEA headquarters. Previously held the DT fusion energy record (59 MJ in 2022). UKAEA and Eni launched Rh3ova (Jul 2, 2026), a joint venture for fusion fuel-cycle consultancy and tritium/deuterium services, complementing the H3AT Tritium Loop Facility. MAST Upgrade completed its fifth experimental campaign (Aug 6, 2026): 1,100+ plasmas, a record plasma pressure without destabilization, and ELM suppression via four independent methods including a world-first use of 3D magnetic coils.

label: Max-Planck IPP — Garching, Germany
sub: ASDEX Upgrade tokamak. Theoretical plasma physics research. Partner in Wendelstein 7-X and EUROfusion consortium.

label: CFETR Site — Hefei, China
sub: China Fusion Engineering Test Reactor. Planned completion ~2035. Target: 2 GW peak output. Adjacent to EAST facility. ASIPP's CRAFT campus in Hefei completed testing of a 582-tonne toroidal field magnet — the largest ever built for fusion — for the next-gen BEST tokamak (Jun 27, 2026); 1.3x the volume and ~3x the stored energy of the equivalent ITER coil, built entirely with domestic components.

label: ENN Group Fusion — Langfang, China
sub: China's leading private fusion venture. Hydrogen-boron FRC approach. EXL-50U achieved 1MA plasma current (2024). EHL-2 under construction.

label: Zap Energy — Seattle, WA
sub: Z-pinch fusion (no magnets). New CEO Zabrina Johal (Apr 2026). Dual fission-fusion strategy: adding 50 MW SMRs for near-term revenue. $160M+ raised. University of Washington spinoff.

label: Marvel Fusion — Munich, Germany
sub: Laser-driven inertial fusion. €113M Series B raised (2024). European private fusion pioneer.

label: NIF Ignition — Dec 5, 2022
sub: Historic ignition shot: 3.15 MJ fusion output from 2.05 MJ laser input. First-ever fusion ignition in a laboratory. Q=1.5 target gain.

label: Stellarex Energy — Toronto, Canada
sub: Princeton University spinoff developing compact stellarator fusion. Signed MOU with UKAEA (May 13, 2026) and Max-Planck-Institut für Plasmaphysik (2024) for joint HTS magnet, plasma physics, and fuel cycle R&D.

label: Type One Energy — Madison, WI
sub: Developer of the Infinity Two stellarator (400 MWe). Active projects: TVA Bull Run site (Tennessee, targeting commercial operations 2034) and UK Infinity Fusion Consortium (announced May 2026 with Tokamak Energy and AECOM). On Aug 5, 2026, ORNL licensed four cryogenic pellet-fueling technologies to Type One Energy to support Infinity One's D-T fueling systems.

label: TAE Beam UK — Culham Campus, UK
sub: TAE Technologies / UKAEA joint venture launched May 14, 2026. UKAEA invested £5.6M. Commercializes neutral beam injection and particle accelerator technology for fusion and non-fusion markets (food safety, cancer therapy, homeland security). Based at Culham Science Centre, Oxfordshire.

label: Fuse Energy Technologies — San Leandro, CA
sub: Builds pulsed-power dense plasma focus (DPF) machines, generating near-term revenue from radiation-effects testing for defense and space customers while advancing toward commercial fusion. Its FAETON-X device reported a peak yield of 1.27×10¹² D-D neutrons per shot (Aug 10, 2026) — the company's claimed highest publicly documented neutron yield by any private fusion company.
